issues.description: Fix only normalizes ClassName nodes — IDs, attributes, type selectors with escapes still slip through
issues.detail: The bug is about CSS escape equivalence. CSS escaping applies to identifiers everywhere — ids (`#u-m\+` vs `#u-m\00002b`), attribute values (`[data-x=u-m\+]`), pseudo-class arguments, custom property-ish idents, type/tag idents. The patch only handles `parser.isClassName(node)`. The same false negative exists for every other identifier the selector parser exposes a value getter/setter on. You fixed one column of a multi-column bug. Either widen the normalization (isClassName || isIdentifier || isAttribute || isTag — whatever the parser exposes setters on) or document explicitly why classes are the only case and file the rest. As shipped, this earns three more bug reports next month.

issues.description: Tests cover only the class case the patch handles — no coverage for ids, attributes, or non-duplicates that must stay non-duplicates
issues.detail: Reject cases are all `.u-m\xx` class duplicates. There is no test that `#u-m\+` and `#u-m\00002b` are (or aren't) duplicates, no attribute selector test, no negative test proving that `.u-m\+` and `.u-mx` don't false-positive after normalization, no test that escape-bearing selectors still report correct columns when surrounded by other selectors. The test set proves the happy path of the one branch that was implemented. Add a few negatives and a few non-class identifiers — either they pass (great, document) or they fail and the scope of the fix expands.

issues.description: `node.value = node.value` self-assign relies on undocumented side-effect of a third-party setter
issues.detail: The trick works because postcss-selector-parser's ClassName setter re-encodes through its escape routine. That is a library internal. If postcss-selector-parser ever changes that getter/setter to be a plain field (perf cleanup, refactor), this normalization silently becomes a no-op and the bug returns with zero test failure noise — because the parser will then return the already-equal raw values for trivial cases but not for the escape-mismatch case. Either wrap with a small helper that asserts the setter actually normalized (e.g. compare raws after), or pin a behavior test against postcss-selector-parser so a future upgrade trips a test, not a user.

issues.description: `@ts-expect-error` masks a real type gap; eslint-disable line buries the intent
issues.detail: Two suppressions in five lines. The `raws.value` check is a perf shortcut piggybacking on an untyped field — fine, but the comment claims `raws` exists; if so, augment the type locally or use a typed accessor rather than perpetually carrying `@ts-expect-error`. The self-assign disable is the right call but combined with the ts-expect-error in the same tiny function it reads like 'we got it working, move on.' For a util that runs on every selector in every lint, the right thing is a 4-line helper with one suppression and a real test that locks in the assumption.

issues.description: Perf: normalizeNodeEscaping now runs for every node in every selector tree on every lint run
issues.detail: `normalizeSelector` is hot — it gets called per rule, per pass. Adding a `parser.isClassName` typecheck plus a `node.raws?.value` access for every walked node is cheap, but it is unmeasured. For a project that lints multi-thousand-rule stylesheets, the early-return on `!node.raws?.value` is doing real work; good. But a one-line benchmark note in the PR (or in the commit message) showing this isn't a regression on a big real stylesheet would be the cost of a coffee. As written: probably fine, but unverified.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch is small, scoped, and the trick — exploiting postcss-selector-parser's getter/setter to renormalize escapes — is genuinely clever and arguably good taste: it eliminates the special-case escape comparison by piggybacking on the parser's own canonical form rather than rolling a bespoke unescape. The diff is readable and matches the surrounding code's voice. What's wrong: the fix is gated on `isClassName`, but the bug class (CSS escape equivalence) lives on every identifier the selector grammar accepts — ids, attributes, idents — and there are no tests proving those cases either pass (free win, document it) or fail (so the scope of the fix is honest). The self-assign normalization relies on undocumented library internals with no behavior test pinning it; one upstream refactor and the bug silently returns. Tighten the surface (more node kinds or an explicit scope justification), add a couple of negative tests, and add one test that locks in the parser-setter behavior. Then it lands.
